### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **60** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), knowledgeSources (symbol, a field of const object STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE), knowledgeSources (literal, a string literal in knowledge))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via admitAuthoredSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), openWriter (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeService (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), KnowledgeSourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const), PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS (symbol, a top-level const object), deploymentAdapter (symbol, a field of interface KnowledgeServiceOptions; a field of interface KnowledgeServicePluginOptions), handleRecordDelete (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), knowledgeSources (symbol, a field of const object STACK_DEFINITION_COLLECTIONS_SHAPE), mountedBy (symbol, a field of interface PlatformCapabilityProvider), registerSource (symbol, a method of class KnowledgeService), getAdapter (literal, a string literal in KnowledgeReapGuardService), knowledgeSources (literal, a string literal in knowledge), registerSource (literal, a string literal in registerSource))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS (symbol, a top-level const object), PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_ERROR (literal, 39 pages)`, `os serve (command, 52 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **196** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bef19fa23959bf5c4fb4cf153a5782957f6d4c7e` — the merge of head `6881aa6f0b2d357a81c79e34f8b19f417c334c0b` into base `6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bef19fa23959bf5c4fb4cf153a5782957f6d4c7e && git checkout bef19fa23959bf5c4fb4cf153a5782957f6d4c7e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c 6881aa6f0b2d357a81c79e34f8b19f417c334c0b && git checkout -B drift-repro 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c && git merge --no-ff 6881aa6f0b2d357a81c79e34f8b19f417c334c0b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6e2a8f2bb577b9fff5225a1280bc6cbbea680c7c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aba523a3413298d11c6b2d54bf02b716f7581abb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/core/src/capability-composition.ts, packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/verify/src/required-providers.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-build-actions.ts, packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-reap-guard.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-authoring.ts

Inputs read: card #37306 (body and all six comments, dev report 7224020195 last), split card #37983 (body, ruling 7220511579, claim, dev report), PR #38026 body and file list, the net diff from merge base `4af32b99db` to the head (23 files, +697/-76), ADR-0161 K4, K6, K8, K10 at the head, and the check-runs on the head (read 2026-11-27T17:16Z). The tests, the two docs pages, the two generated reference pages and the changeset prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT; they were read only to judge the files above.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.

1. `KnowledgeSourceSchema.adapter`: `z.string()` to `z.string().optional()`. RIGHT, a widening. Every value that parsed still parses and reads the same (a named adapter is kept as written); a non-string is still refused. The new accepted spelling is the omitted key. Nothing that parsed on `main` is refused.
2. Reader-side type: `KnowledgeSource['adapter']` becomes `string | undefined`. RIGHT, and inherent in item 1. Every reader in the tree was moved or already tolerant: the service's twelve call sites go through `adapterIdFor` / `adapterFor` / `boundAdapterId`; `packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/status.ts` already prints `?? '?'`; `rebuild.ts` compares the placed adapter that `index_status` now answers. No adapter package reads the field. A grep of the head for a remaining direct read found only the two guarded lines in `reportUnmountedAdapters`.
3. `PlatformCapabilityProvider.mountedBy?` (new optional member) and the `knowledge` row carrying it. RIGHT as an addition; one part of its shape is not (S1 in section ④).
4. `stackItemCapabilities` (new export of `@objectstack/core`), `resolveServedCapabilities` option `itemTokens`, `ServedCapabilities.byItems`, and the `knowledge` branch of `resolveCapabilityArgument`. RIGHT. `byItems` is a new required member of a returned type: additive for every reader.
5. `KnowledgeServicePluginOptions.deploymentAdapter?` and `KnowledgeServiceOptions.deploymentAdapter?`. RIGHT. A service option, as ADR-0161 K8 ("Not members": an option of the service) and the card's item 2 require. `IKnowledgeAdapter` and `registerAdapter` are untouched, so application code cannot mark its own adapter by registering.
6. New methods on `KnowledgeService`: `adapterIdFor`, `adapterFor`, `boundAdapterId`. RIGHT, additive.
7. `KnowledgeIndexStatusEntry.adapter` from `string` to `adapter?: string`. RIGHT. It is absent only for a source that names no adapter and cannot be placed, a state that cannot exist on `main`; every answer `main` gives keeps the field.
8. New refusals: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` at `registerSource`, at the loader door and at `admitAuthoredSource`, and at index and search for a source left unplaceable later; `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` where no adapter is registered. RIGHT, and none is a hidden narrowing: each fires only for a source with no `adapter`, which `main` refuses at parse. The loader catches the throw per item and reports it once, so one refused item does not stop the listing.
9. A stack that ships a `knowledge_source` and lists no `requires: ['knowledge']` is now served the service and one store, as a declared token. RIGHT against ADR-0161 K8 item 12. Does anything that ran before now refuse? Read for it: `@objectstack/service-knowledge` is a hard dependency of the CLI and of verify, so the import cannot be missing; the turso store is an optional extra whose import failure is a warning; the pgvector store's `start()` warns on a failed health check and does not throw. So the boot of such a stack does not fail where it booted before. What does change for it is stated in N1.
10. MCP draft door, `itemSaveRefusal`: a verdict that is not a 403 keeps its own code. RIGHT. On `main` every verdict of the platform's admitter that is not a 403 is `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (read: every `refuse(` in `admitAuthoredSource` is 403, and `unavailable` is 503), so no answer an MCP client gets today changes; only this PR's new 400 is affected. The three save doors now agree: REST passes `refused.code`, the dispatcher derives `VALIDATION_ERROR` from status 400 (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`), MCP passes the code.

Hidden narrowing: none found in what an author can write or in what a deployment runs. Two TypeScript-only tightenings exist on helper types of `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, recorded as N5.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: RIGHT. The published schema accepts one more spelling and refuses none.
- `Metadata-protocol: added`: RIGHT. A newly accepted value (the omitted `adapter`) is `added` by the AGENTS.md definition. The item mount does not move the meaning or the default of any authorable key: a named `adapter` and a listed `requires` read as before, and an item with no reader was a reported fault on `main` (row 3a's boot line, ADR-0078), which ADR-0161 K8 item 12 decided to end. So neither `semantic` nor `narrowed` applies, and the precedence rule changes nothing.
- Bookkeeping `added` owes: a level of at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, and no ADR-0087 disposition (ADR-0161 K4 and K6: "widens what an author may write and takes no disposition"; the registration gate reads `added` as no signal). Present: `@objectstack/spec` is `minor`, and both declaration lines stand in the changeset body and the PR body. `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness` and the lint gate families that carry the generated-artifact and surface checks concluded success on this head. The two regenerated reference pages are in the diff.
- Levels, package by package: `spec` minor (new accepted value, new interface member), `core` minor (new export, new option, new returned member), `service-knowledge` minor (new option and methods), `cli` and `verify` minor (new mount behaviour) are RIGHT. `runtime` patch is RIGHT: a corrected error code for a verdict that cannot occur before this PR, no protocol kind of its own.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #37310` is consistent with the card's fence (`skills/**` is row 5b's).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Declared deviation, the runtime `mcp-authoring.ts` mapping. In scope of the card, not an adjacent defect: the card's item 1 adds a refusal at the save, and this is that refusal reaching an existing door correctly. Without the edit the PR's own `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` would arrive over MCP as `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with status 400. Read as an adjacent in-place fix it still holds on each count: it is reachable only through this PR's change, it is one expression with no new surface, it is declared in the PR body and carries a `runtime` patch entry, and it is pinned (the new case in `mcp-authoring.test.ts`; ablation A11 reported red with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` where `VALIDATION_ERROR` was expected). It is right: parity with the REST door, read in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts`. See N4 for the cast.
- The two semantic-conflict fixes with `main`. Both read in the head. The boot pass (`buildIfDue`, from 205f667ec0) now skips a source at boot when `boundAdapterId` answers nothing or names an adapter that is not registered, which is the same set `reportUnmountedAdapters` names once at `error`; the comment and the code agree. The reconcile (`reconcileExclusion`, from merge 635fb18bc5) reads the adapter the source is placed on before it asks for `listDocuments`; an unplaced source falls through and is walked, so its build fails and names it, as the method's own doc says for an adapter that is not mounted. Both are this card's change meeting a new reader of the field it made optional; fixing them here is correct, and leaving them would not compile. Pins exist for both (A9, A10 reported red).
- Overlap with #37963 (open draft). Its patch was read: one textual hunk in the admitted-sources loop of `knowledge-service.ts`. Its added lines read the adapter from the plan it is handed and add no new direct read of `source.adapter`. No semantic conflict; whoever lands second keeps both edits.
- Overlap with #38015. Its patch was read: it appends one sentence to six tombstone prescriptions in `knowledge-source.zod.ts`, none on the `adapter` line, and regenerates `content/docs/references/ai/knowledge-source.mdx`. The source edits do not meet; only the generated page does, and it is regenerated on the merged tree. Nothing else conflicts semantically.
- `Fixes #37306` with item 4 elsewhere. The card closes rightly. Item 4 and its acceptance line live on #37983, whose body records the seat's split and whose ruling 7220511579 (the maintainer's D) replaces item 4's two options. Once this PR lands nothing of #37306 remains to do, so `Part of` would leave a card open with no work. The PR-body guard concluded success. One record gap: N6.
- `check:type-check-debt`, NOT MEASURED locally. Covered: the check-run `Type Check · debt ledger` concluded success on this head.
- Check-runs on the head at 17:16Z: 26 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 31 in progress (`Test Core` 1 to 10, `Test UI` 1 to 16, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`). This record judges the contract; those conclusions remain the gate verdicts and the queue reads them.
- PostgreSQL acceptance, NOT MEASURED locally. The PR body names `capability-mount.live-postgres.test.ts` as CI's cover. That file, unchanged by this diff, writes `adapter: 'pgvector'` and `requires: ['knowledge']`, so it exercises neither the omitted adapter nor the item mount. What pins the card's second acceptance line is the composition of two unit pins: `resolveCapabilityArgument('knowledge', postgres)` answers `{ deploymentAdapter: 'pgvector' }`, and a source with no adapter binds to the marked store. Handed to the lane seat's ACCEPT as N2.
- Dev open questions: report 7224020195 carries none. The earlier ones (item 4, the landing order against #37963, the #37982 bullet, #38015) are each answered by a ruling the later reports carry out.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join in this diff. Placement is a map lookup over registered adapters.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts`. Holds against ADR-0161 K4. The jsdoc and the `describe` text say: omitted means the store the runtime mounted beside the service, else the only adapter registered, and several with none the deployment's is refused naming them. `adapterIdFor` does exactly that, in that order. Tried to break it: (a) a source registered in code at `init()` before any store started is taken and placed at use, so the ADR's "refused at registration" is deferred only where the registry is not yet final; (b) a mark with its store absent and nothing else gives 503 naming the store; (c) two adapters with no mark is refused at both doors and at the save. First consumer: BrightRule mounts the service by hand and names its adapter; `serve.ts` skips both the provider and the extras when the host holds the service (`hasPluginMatching`), so it gets no store and no mark and is unchanged.

`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`. The `knowledgeSources` description now says the CLI mounts the service where the stack holds a source or lists the token. `serve.ts` and `required-providers.ts` do so through one rule.

`packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`.

S1 (should-fix) — `mountedBy.type` ships with no reader. The new member is `{ collection, type }` and the `knowledge` row sets `type: 'knowledge_source'`, but `stackItemCapabilities` reads `collection` alone; a grep of the head finds `type` only in the row and in a test that asserts its literal value. The member's own jsdoc describes the collection and never says what `type` is for. It is also a second statement of a fact the spec already owns: `packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts` maps `knowledgeSources` to `knowledge_source`, so the two can drift with nothing to notice. ADR-0161 K10 rule 1 (a key lands with its first reader in the same PR) and the K8 note on what is not a member ("they land with their reader") both apply to a required field of a published interface on a governed path. Its reader appears to have left with item 4. Fix before it publishes, since removing it later narrows a published type: drop `type` and keep `mountedBy: { collection }`, or land it with a reader and a doc line; a later reader can derive the type from the spelling map.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence.

- `capability-composition.ts`, `capability-providers.ts`: the mark is `resolveKnowledgeStore(input).store.adapterId`, the same call `resolveCapabilityExtras` mounts from, on the same `database` input in both boots, so the mark and the mounted store cannot disagree. Item tokens are appended after the declared ones and counted as declared, as the changeset says.
- `serve.ts`, `required-providers.ts`: both pass `itemTokens` and the same `database` to the argument and to the extras. Agree with the contract.
- `knowledge-service.ts`, `knowledge-service-plugin.ts`, `knowledge-build-actions.ts`, `knowledge-reap-guard.ts`: agree with the spec text; every former `getAdapter(source.adapter)` site was moved.
- `mcp-authoring.ts`: agrees with its comment and with the REST door.

Nits. None changes correctness or the contract; a fix that moves a reviewed file is left to a follow-up.

N1 — The changeset's "What to do: nothing" omits one case. A stack on 19.0.0-next.1 that ships a source without `requires: ['knowledge']` held an inert item with a boot warning; after this change the service mounts and the boot pass builds its index, which sends content to the embedder where one is configured (ADR-0161 K5: embedding is egress). That is the decided behaviour of K8 item 12, on a prerelease line, and the changeset's first paragraph states the mount. One sentence in the changeset and PR body for that reader would close it (prose face).

N2 — The PR body's sentence that CI covers the PostgreSQL acceptance through `capability-mount.live-postgres.test.ts` overstates: that test names the adapter and the token. Correct the sentence (prose face) and carry a follow-up that drops `adapter` and `requires` from the live case, so the card's second acceptance line is exercised end to end.

N3 — `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts` composes "what `os serve` mounts" from `resolveServedCapabilities(requires)` without `itemTokens`, so `os migrate plan` on an item-only stack does not compose the knowledge service. No effect today: the service declares no objects. Follow-up, so the two boots stay one rule.

N4 — `refused.code as ErrorCode` is an unchecked cast of a duck-typed service's string; the code before it clamped every such answer to `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. The REST door passes the string through the same way, so this is parity, and the platform's admitter answers ledger codes only. A guard against a code outside the vocabulary is a follow-up for both doors.

N5 — Two helper types of `@objectstack/service-knowledge` ask one more member of a hand-built service object: `KnowledgeBuildActionsService` (the parameter of the exported `knowledgeIndexStatusActionHandler`) gains `boundAdapterId`, and the reap guard's pick swaps `getAdapter` for `adapterFor`. A caller that passes the real `KnowledgeService`, which is every caller in the tree, is unaffected; the compiler carries it for a stub (ADR-0087 D7). Accepted as is.

N6 — #37306's own thread carries no seat line recording the split of item 4; only the dev reports and #37983's body say so, and the card body still lists item 4 and its acceptance line. One seat comment on #37306 naming #37983 and ruling 7220511579 before the merge closes the card (prose face).

N7 — Two message details. `noAdapterMountedError` advises "`requires: ['knowledge']` mounts the deployment's" even in the branch where a mark is set, which means the capability was already requested and the remedy is installing the optional store package. And with a mark set whose store is not registered, a source with no adapter binds to the only other adapter registered; that follows the ADR's words ("or the only adapter registered"), but during startup it can place an early record sync on an application adapter before the runtime's store registers. The boot pass and the reconcile repair it. Follow-up.

N8 — The `vectorStore` tombstone in `knowledge-source.zod.ts` still says the store is "named by `adapter`"; with the key optional that is true only where it is named. Not touched by this diff; a wording follow-up.

Open on this head: S1.

## 席位核对

**Contract review.** Record 7224273377 at this head: PASS at the contract tier (`verify-review-tier` PASS), with one graded finding, S1, which the queue guard reads as open. I adopt the record. It rules all six of the area's points the way the PR declares: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are right, the `itemSaveRefusal` mapping is in scope and pinned, both semantic-conflict fixes are right, the overlaps with #37963 and #38015 are textual only, `Fixes #37306` is right given ruling 7220511579 on #37983, and `Type Check · debt ledger` is green in CI.

**S1, confirmed on the tree.** `mountedBy.type` (`platform-capabilities.ts:175`, set to `'knowledge_source'` at :255) has no reader. `stackItemCapabilities` reads only `.collection` (`capability-composition.ts:100`), and the one other mention is a test asserting the literal. A published spec key that nothing reads goes against ADR-0161 K10 rule 1. It also duplicates the `knowledgeSources` to `knowledge_source` mapping that `meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts` already owns. **Next head:** drop `type` from the row type and the row, along with the test literal and any generated reference. Or, if item 4 (#37983) needs it, land it there with its reader and a jsdoc line.

**Same head, optional prose (record nits):**
- N1: the changeset's "What to do: nothing" should say that a 19.0.0-next.1 stack shipping a source without `requires` goes from inert to indexed, embedding through the configured embedder.
- N2: correct the PR body's claim about `capability-mount.live-postgres.test.ts`.
- N6: one comment on #37306 naming the item-4 split (#37983, ruling 7220511579).
- N3, N4, N5, N7 and N8 stand as accepted deviations or follow-ups.

**CI.** At 17:16Z, Test Core, Test UI, Type Check (workspace and consumer gates) and the E2E lanes were still running. The next head needs them green.

**Next:** a new head, a delta L2 on S1, a delta L1, then the seat's Tier H handoff (protocol-added).

`packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts`, the migrate boot. Judged as a behaviour change. What `os migrate plan` / `apply` now composes that it did not: `KnowledgeServicePlugin`, for a stack that ships a `knowledge_source` and lists no `knowledge` token. What that does during a migrate run, read in the head:

- It is composed through `composeProviderForDeclarations`: `init()` runs, `start()` is suppressed, and `init()` can register no lifecycle hook at all, `kernel:ready` included. The declaration boot's write guard refuses row writes.
- `KnowledgeServicePlugin.init()` builds the service object, registers it under `knowledge`, and contributes the knowledge settings. It opens no connection and calls no network.
- Everything with an effect lives in `start()` and in the `kernel:bootstrapped` hook `start()` registers: loading published sources, providing the embedder, the boot build pass, the reconcile job, the record-sync subscription. None of it runs.
- No store is composed. This loop reads the row's `extras`, and the `knowledge` row of `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` has none (serve takes the store from `resolveCapabilityExtras`). So no libSQL file is created and no PostgreSQL pool is opened.
- The plugin gets no argument (no posture row), so no mark is set; nothing reads one in a declaration boot.
- It cannot newly fail: `@objectstack/service-knowledge` is a hard dependency of the CLI, and this loop does not use the `declared` set.
- The path is not new. A stack that lists `requires: ['knowledge']` already composed the same plugin the same way on `main`; the change extends that to the item-only stack.

So nothing is opened, embedded, built, scheduled or sent. The service declares no objects, so a plan is the same as before; the one visible difference is that the "Composed what `os serve` mounts" note now lists `KnowledgeServicePlugin`. The change is right for the reason the parity pin exists: both boots compose one set from one rule. Pins: `stackItemCapabilities` is a named step of `boot-preparation-parity.test.ts`, and the behaviour case has an item-only stack and an app-only control (A12 reported red without the option).
